valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 27 Nov 2026. (1) Business: three companies, weighted by their share of 2025/26 group operating profit (Annual Report 2025/26, p. 79): Hayleys Fibre PLC (coir fibre, coco-peat grow bags and substrates for horticulture) 25%, Bonterra (coir erosion-control blankets and geotextiles for infrastructure projects) 39%, Creative Polymats (foam and coir mattresses for Sri Lanka) 36%. (2) Damodaran's emerging-markets dataset (betaEmerg) could NOT be opened: his site is blocked by this run's network settings. Stand-ins are the global unlevered, cash-corrected figures other analyses on this site already use from web-search extracts: Farming/Agriculture 0.49 (growing media), Building Materials 0.90 (erosion control for construction), Household Products 0.77 (mattresses). Weighted: 0.25 × 0.49 + 0.39 × 0.90 + 0.36 × 0.77 = 0.75. (3) Relevered with net debt Rs 2.540bn at 30 Sep 2026 (borrowings 2.894 + leases 0.005 − cash 0.359, Interim to 30 Sep 2026, p. 5) ÷ market value Rs 3.678bn (24.0mn shares × Rs 153.25, last trade 30 Sep 2026) = 0.69, at the 2025/26 tax rate of 32.4%: 0.75 × (1 + 0.676 × 0.69) = 1.10. (4) No local 5-year beta found by web search; the share traded thinly until 2025 (6,027 trades in 2024/25, p. 251), so a local beta would be unreliable anyway. (5) So 1.10. (6) Within 0.3–2. (7) Cost of equity from scripts/reinvestment.py. (8) Shown in the Required return tile. Refresh in January 2027 with the emerging-markets file.

valuationInputs.name: WACC
valuationInputs.reason: scripts/reinvestment.py, 27 Nov 2026: cost of debt 8.01% (interest paid Rs 154mn ÷ average borrowings and leases 2025/26), tax 32.4%, debt weight 40.9% at Rs 153.25. Used only in the DCF cross-check.

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 2% / 5% / 8%; supported 31.3% by the calculator, 14.5% on profit kept × ROE
valuationInputs.reason: The calculator's figure comes from a 2025/26 reinvestment rate of 262% (a Rs 719mn working-capital build: receivables, stock and amounts due from affiliates) and isn't meaningful. Profit kept × ROE (100% kept, no dividend, × the company's 14.5% ROE for 2025/26, p. 20) = 14.5%: all scenarios are within it.

valuationInputs.name: Maintenance capex basis
valuationInputs.reason: No company split. 2025/26 capex booked Rs 256mn (PPE additions 249.5 + work in progress 6.3) against depreciation and amortisation Rs 93mn; the report ties the building spending to the new Nikaweratiya plant (pp. 26, 85), so the year's capex was mostly growth. The 'Rs 64mn incurred on maintenance and upkeep' (p. 48) is a running cost, not capex.

valuationInputs.name: Methods used
valuationInputs.value: P/E, justified price to book, residual income (weighted); whole-company DCF as a cross-check
valuationInputs.reason: Operating cash was negative in 2025/26 (−Rs 361mn) and H1 2026/27 (−Rs 392mn), so the DCF needs a normalised start and, with Rs 2.54bn of net debt against a Rs 3.7bn market value, swings from Rs −80 to Rs 78 a share. No dividends for three years, so no dividend model.

valuationInputs.name: EPS to March 2027
valuationInputs.reason: H1 Rs 4.86 (Interim to 30 Sep 2026, p. 1) plus a second half of Rs 2.6 / 4.6 / 6.1; the second half of 2025/26 earned Rs 5.45 (7.13 − 1.68) with cyclone replacement demand and a government mattress tender. Run-rate Rs 10.31 (last 12 months; Sep quarter × 4 Rs 2.96): base 8% below it because the September quarter earned only Rs 0.74 and finance costs doubled.

valuationInputs.name: Long-run ROE
valuationInputs.reason: Owners' ROE 17%, 23%, −2%, −3% and 12% for 2021/22–2025/26 (EPS and equity, ten-year summary p. 239), about 9% on average; ten-year average about 11% (EPS ÷ NAV); last 12 months 16.3%.

valuationInputs.name: Long-term growth
valuationInputs.reason: Roughly nominal GDP growth; below the 12.24% bond yield and WACC.

valuationInputs.name: DCF cross-check inputs
valuationInputs.value: Start cash Rs 0.21 / 0.40 / 0.44bn; after-tax operating profit Rs 0.43bn; growth 2 / 5 / 8%; return on capital 10 / 13 / 16%
valuationInputs.reason: Last 12 months' operating profit Rs 0.636bn at the 32.4% tax rate, plus depreciation Rs 0.104bn, less maintenance capex Rs 0.33 / 0.14 / 0.09bn (calculator range); working-capital growth charged through reinvestment. Result Rs −80 / 11 / 78 a share before minorities, not weighted.

valuationInputs.name: Payout
valuationInputs.reason: No dividend for 2023/24–2025/26 (ten-year summary p. 239; p. 86); 49% and 31% in 2021/22 and 2022/23. Assumes a partial return to dividends over the ten years.

openQuestions: Does operating cash turn positive in the second half, and do receivables (Rs 1.71bn) and amounts due from Hayleys affiliates (Rs 1.03bn) come down?
Was the September quarter's weak profit (EPS Rs 0.74) a one-off, or are higher finance costs and raw-material prices squeezing margins?
Net debt Rs 2.54bn at Sep 2026: does it fall back towards owners' equity by March 2027?
Creative Polymats capacity expansion: amount and timing (not stated).
Dividend: any resumption with the March 2027 results?
Split of profit between Hayleys Fibre, Bonterra and Creative Polymats (no segment note in the interims).
Refresh the beta in January 2027 with Damodaran's emerging-markets file and any local 5-year betas; switch to the CSE close once HEXP is in the price file.

changeLog.summary: Requested from Telegram (/add HEXP.N0000). First analysis, from the downloaded annual report 2025/26 and the interims to June and September 2026. Methods: P/E, justified price to book and residual income at a 19.5% cost of equity (beta 1.10, provisional, global stand-ins for agriculture, building materials and household products); DCF as a cross-check only because operating cash was negative. Business tests 0 of 4: category 3, avoid for now. Uncertain: price is the last trade at 30 Sep 2026 (Rs 153.25) printed in the interim, as the CSE site and price websites couldn't be reached and HEXP isn't in the price file; no local 5-year beta; no segment split in the interims; operating cash for 2021/22–2023/24 not in the reports read; R&D not disclosed.
